amendments.note: Added 21 Nov: Inkling 2 Mini with thinking on (effort 0.9), under the same rule, lesson prompt, test and schedule, on the server it shares with Logic & Math and other benchmarks (its owner's pinned load; this run neither starts nor stops it), sampled greedily as on Logic & Math (temperature 0), its first empty test a validity check as above. Its letter is read from its own answer after its reasoning: its server cannot continue a prefilled answer after a reasoning block. While that server is away, the model pauses. At effort 0.9, 110 of the first 148 answers used all 32,768 output tokens without naming an option; that run stopped and played no series. It was then rerun at effort 0.5, otherwise unchanged. That rerun also stopped at the validity check: 40 of 200 answers (20%) used all 32,768 output tokens without naming an option, above the 10% invalid-answer limit; it played no series.

Inkling 2 Mini retry order, decided before either retry's first call. A capped answer counts as a trailing loop when a pattern of at most 64 whitespace tokens reproduces at least 80% of its final 512 whitespace tokens. Of the capped answers, effort 0.9 had 31 loops and 79 still reasoning normally; effort 0.5 had 25 loops and 15 still reasoning normally. Combined, 56 of 150 were loops and 94 were still reasoning normally, so the lower-effort retry comes first. First try: effort 0.2, temperature 0 and the same 32,768-token limit. Its first empty run is the 200-position validity check; at most 20 invalid answers passes, then this setup plays the full schedule. If it fails, second try: effort 0.5 with the model card's complete sampling configuration (do_sample true, temperature 1.0, eos token 200006 and pad token 199999; the token ids are properties of the loaded server, and the request changes temperature from 0 to 1.0). The card specifies no top_p, top_k or min_p. This is a different setup from the Logic & Math row, which uses effort 0.9 and temperature 0. Sampling at temperature 1.0 can widen this setup's own three-empty-run spread and therefore raise its improvement threshold. Its first empty run uses the same validity check; if it passes, it plays the full schedule. If both retries fail, Inkling stops and is recorded as unable to take the test; there is no third setting. Exploratory 10-position probe, not a result: effort 0.9 with the card's temperature 1.0 returned 9 valid answers and had 1 answer reach the 32,768-token limit; mean output was about 19,500 tokens, median about 16,000 and the slowest request took 814 seconds. The probe was effort 0.9, not the second retry's effort 0.5. On 24 Nov, after Logic & Math's shared server was gone, Learning loaded one compatible copy on its reserved GPU 2 from the same pinned revision, image and server arguments. Logic disabled its pending GPU 1 copy; the GPU 3 small-model lane was not interrupted. The live load is shared with Logic, Compactor, Jack and Toolbench, which do not stop or restart it. Same-day Learning decision: Inkling keeps this evidence and first-retry priority. LFM2.5-24B-A2B thinking off runs on our GPU immediately after Qwen3.5-2B, with the 200-position validity check (at most 20 invalid passes) and the existing context-fit stop rule; lessons are never shortened. Four reasoning-high successors were planned at this decision: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol through the ChatGPT subscription with no explicit output-cap override; Gemini 4 Neon through Antigravity, thinking high with no explicit output-cap override; Claude Fable 5.2 through a separate Claude subscription, adaptive thinking at effort high with a 32,768-token output limit. Estimated full schedules: Astra / Sol about 2,700 requests and $180–$200 / $45–$50 API-list-price equivalent; Neon about 2,900 and $405–$410; Fable about 2,900 and $440–$445. These scale predecessor usage at current standard API input/output prices per million tokens: Astra $8/$40, Sol $2/$10, Neon $3/$15, Fable $8/$40; they are not quota guarantees. The later 24 Nov amendment records their approved starts.
